article_title: MoD data breach a 'foreseeable' failure that left Afghans in danger, inquiry finds

tasks.prompt: What was the parliamentary inquiry's central conclusion about the MoD data breach?
options: It was an unavoidable cyberattack carried out by the Taliban
It exposed no more information than the MoD intended
It was a foreseeable systemic failure worsened by weak procedures and secrecy
It concerned only routine immigration data with no safety consequences
tasks.correct_answer: It was a foreseeable systemic failure worsened by weak procedures and secrecy
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הוועדה קבעה שלא מדובר רק בטעות אישית אלא בכשל מערכתי שניתן היה לצפותו, על רקע נהלים, הכשרה ותרבות ארגונית לקויים.

tasks.prompt: How did hidden information for more than 18,500 applications become exposed?
options: A staff member shared an Excel spreadsheet believed to contain data for about 150 applicants
Applicants deliberately posted their own records on social media
Parliament published the full relocation database
A foreign government stole a paper archive from an embassy
tasks.correct_answer: A staff member shared an Excel spreadsheet believed to contain data for about 150 applicants
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בגיליון שנשלח לצד שלישי מהימן נראו לכאורה כ־150 רשומות, אך הוסתר בו מידע על יותר מ־18,500 בקשות נוספות.

tasks.prompt: What prevented the public from learning about the breach until July 2025?
options: A strike by civil servants
The loss of every copy of the spreadsheet
A parliamentary election campaign
An unprecedented superinjunction
tasks.explanation_hebrew: צו מניעה חריג במיוחד מנע פרסום של הפרשה עד יולי 2025, אף שהמידע דלף שנים קודם לכן.

tasks.prompt: Why does the inquiry call the breach “systemic” rather than merely an individual mistake?
options: Because only one spreadsheet program can ever be used securely
Because multiple organisational weaknesses contributed, including tools, procedures, training and culture
Because every government department sent the same email
Because no identifiable person handled the data
tasks.correct_answer: Because multiple organisational weaknesses contributed, including tools, procedures, training and culture
tasks.explanation_hebrew: systemic פירושו מערכתי: הכשל נבע משילוב ליקויים רחב בארגון ולא מפעולה מבודדת בלבד.

tasks.prompt: The committee said secrecy was used as a “shield against accountability”. What does this metaphor imply?
options: Secrecy physically protected applicants from the Taliban
Classified operations made all administrative decisions automatically lawful
Claims of secrecy were used to avoid scrutiny and responsibility
Parliament demanded that all relocation work remain secret forever
tasks.correct_answer: Claims of secrecy were used to avoid scrutiny and responsibility
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המטפורה מציגה את הסודיות כמגן ששימש להדיפת ביקורת ולמניעת מתן דין וחשבון, גם בנושאים מנהליים.

tasks.prompt: What does “foreseeable” add to the inquiry's criticism?
options: The harm could reasonably have been anticipated and prevented
The breach was discovered before any data was shared
The inquiry predicted the exact date of every later event
The consequences were visible only with hindsight and could not be reduced
tasks.correct_answer: The harm could reasonably have been anticipated and prevented
tasks.explanation_hebrew: foreseeable מדגיש שהסיכון לא היה בלתי צפוי; ניתן היה לזהותו מראש ולנקוט אמצעי מניעה מתאימים.

tasks.prompt: Why did the committee distinguish secrecy around Special Forces operations from accountability for administrative failures? Answer in 4–6 sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להכיר בצורך להגן על מידע מבצעי, אך להסביר שסודיות זו אינה אמורה למנוע ביקורת על טיפול בנתונים ובבקשות הגירה.
expected_points: Sensitive operational information may legitimately require secrecy
Spreadsheet handling and relocation casework are administrative functions
Operational secrecy should not conceal poor procedures or governance
Parliament and the public still need enough information to assign responsibility

tasks.prompt: Write a 120–170 word summary of the article without copying sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את אופן הדליפה, היקפה, ממצאי הוועדה, צו המניעה והסיכון לאפגנים שעבדו לצד בריטניה.
expected_points: An MoD spreadsheet exposed data linked to more than 18,500 applications
The committee described the breach as foreseeable and systemic
Weak tools, procedures, training and data-protection culture contributed
A superinjunction delayed public disclosure until July 2025
Afghans connected to UK forces faced danger, delay and uncertainty
The inquiry criticised secrecy being used to block accountability

tasks.prompt: Explain in 5–7 sentences why the hidden spreadsheet rows are important evidence for the inquiry's systemic-failure argument.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשר בין הפער העצום בהיקף הנתונים, השימוש בכלי לא מתאים, בדיקות חסרות, הכשרה ותרבות הגנת מידע.
expected_points: The sender apparently believed the file held about 150 visible records
Hidden data covered more than 18,500 additional applications
The scale shows the risk of using spreadsheets without robust controls
Review, training and data-handling procedures failed to catch the danger
The evidence supports an organisational rather than purely personal explanation

tasks.prompt: Assess in 5–7 sentences the inquiry's claim that the MoD should not have been left to run relocation casework schemes.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג את טענת הוועדה, להשתמש בראיות על מומחיות, אבטחת מידע והטיפול בבקשות, ולציין שיקול נגדי אפשרי לפני מסקנה.
expected_points: State the committee's concern about limited immigration-casework expertise
Use evidence from the breach or wrongly refused applications
Explain the consequences for Afghan applicants
Consider whether defence knowledge could still be relevant to some cases
Reach a reasoned conclusion about institutional responsibility
